claims.statement: Badly parked bikes result in escalating rider penalties ranging from warnings to complete account bans.
claims.sourceQuote: Riders who park badly face escalating penalties: a warning, then fines, and bans for repeat offenders.
claims.sourceDocument: Public Transport Liaison Forum Lewisham, 20 October 2026

claims.statement: Lime is exploring artificial intelligence age verification to halt underage riding on its fleet.
claims.sourceQuote: Lime is investigating technological solutions to prevent underage riding, such as AI-powered age verification, which requires riders to scan an ID if the AI detects a risk.
claims.sourceDocument: Public Transport Liaison Forum Lewisham, 20 October 2026

takeawayCard.title: Footway Bays Shift To Carriageways
takeawayCard.subtitle: Lime shifts bays to clear pavements for pedestrians.

keyPoints: Lime is funding new parking bays with prime density around 200 metres.
Riders who park badly face escalating warnings, fines, and permanent service bans.
Lime bikes cap speed at 15 miles per hour while testing AI verification.

onScreenGraphic.headline: How will Lime tackle poor parking?

timeline.voiceoverText: The operator is rolling out new road bays, issuing escalating fines to offenders, and introducing artificial intelligence checks.
With speeds capped at fifteen miles per hour, bays will move from footways to roads to reduce street clutter.
